course_title: Physiotherapy Foundations II: Physiotherapy Practice and Modalities
course_description:
This course provides an opportunity for students to learn the safe application of electrotherapeutic agents and to understand the role and clinical utility of new technologies in the assessment and management of clients.

This course introduces students to therapeutic modalities in physiotherapy and consists of three modules: (1)ﾠclinical observations; (2) digital technologies in health; (3) electrophysical agents.ﾠ

Module 1 ﾠexposes students to physiotherapy practice and work environments. Students will also develop an understanding of Occupational Health and Safety policies and procedures, the National Safety and Quality Health Service Standards and the Physiotherapy practice thresholds, with an emphasis on professional practice and communication.

Module 2 will introduce students to digital technologies and how they can impact on physiotherapy practice. Students will develop an understanding of how contemporary digital technologies can be used in the service delivery of physiotherapy.ﾠﾠ

Module 3 ﾠexposes students to the theoretical aspects of physics and the practical application of electrophysical agents. Students will develop the communication and clinical reasoning skills required for the safe and effective application of electrophysical agents in physiotherapy.ﾠ

course_aims: The aims of this course are to enable the student to:

learning_outcomes.description: Explain the basic functions and therapeutic effects of electrophysical agents used in physiotherapy.
Apply clinical reasoning and evidence-based principles to determine the selection, dosage, and application of electrophysical agents in a safe, culturally responsive, and client-centred manner.
Apply Occupational Health and Safety policies and procedures, and the National Safety and Quality Health Service Standards, to the clinical context.
Reflect on and apply key concepts from the Physiotherapy Practice Thresholds such as cultural safety, professional practice and communication skills to the clinical context.
Apply and integrate contemporary digital technologies into appropriate physiotherapy practice settings, including rural and remote telehealth.
Apply interprofessional practice skills, including role clarification, team functioning, interprofessional communication and client-centred care.

assessment_details.title: IPCP Curriculum Assessment
assessment_details.task_description: Please refer to the assessment information on Learn.UQ for the assessment due date for your team. This is a team assessment, and all team members are expected to contribute equally to the team’s assessment items. Teams will be assigned during your first tutorial. There are three (3) parts to this assessment: Part One requires you to complete a worksheet and will draw on content from Module 1 of the IPCP curriculum focusing on role-clarification and negotiation, and relationship focused care and services. Length: There is no word limit for the worksheet. Part Two involves creating a 3-minute video which draws upon the content from Modules 2 and 3 of the IPCP curriculum focusing on team communication, team functioning and relationship focused care and services. Length: Video 3 minutes. Part Three involves a check-in with a tutor, to assess and reflect on processes of collaboration Length: approx. 10 minutes. Teams will need to submit Parts One and Two of your assessment in the Assessment tab on the HMBS1240 IPCP Learn.UQ course site. Additional information regarding submission will be provided on the HMBS1240 IPCP Learn.UQ course site. Please refer to the assessment information on Learn.UQ for further details and requirements for the assessment. Submission: Online submission via Blackboard. The IPCP module is a Pass/Fail assessment task. Students who pass the module will receive a course grade based on the remaining assessment in the course. • For students who engage with the module, participate in the group work and submit a genuine attempt but do not achieve a pass grade for their submitted work, there will be given a second opportunity to pass the module by completing a reflective essay. If this task is successfully completed, a grade will be awarded based on the remaining assessment in the course. • Students who do not engage with the module, fail to participate in the group work, or do not submit a genuine attempt, will be given an opportunity to complete a 5,000 word assignment on teamwork. Successful completion of this assignment will enable students to then pass the course with a maximum grade of 4 (if the remaining assessment in the course would result in a grade higher than 4, a maximum grade of 4 will be awarded). • Students who fail the module who do not complete either the reflective essay or the teamwork assignment will be awarded a maximum grade of 3 (if the remaining assessment in the course would result in a grade higher than 3, a maximum grade of 3 will be awarded). learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 13
learning_activities.topic: Online modules and lectures A series of online lectures and modules is designed for independent, self-paced learning across Clinical, Digital Technology and Electrophysical Agent topics within this course. These are spread across the entire semester. There are three modules on Telehealth: first module takes approximately 7 hours to complete, the 2nd module takes about 8 hours to complete, and the final module takes about 4.5hours to complete. There are two additional lectures on choosing and using technology in clinical practice that are approximately 1 hour duration each. The clinical modules consist of approximately 5 hours of online content. The electrophysical modules consist of approximately 6 hours of online content. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 2 To Week 11
learning_activities.topic: Interprofessional Collaborative Practice Modules Participants will work in small teams in tutorial groups with students from Dentistry, Exercise Physiology and Sports Science, Midwifery, Nursing, Occupational Therapy, Pharmacy, Physiotherapy, Social Work and Speech Pathology. There are three modules that consist of on-line preparation and face-to-face learning activities. You will work in your team to engage in a range of learning activities to develop your knowledge and skills to help prepare you for working in teams when caring for clients. · In Module One, you will learn about relationship-focused care, role clarification and negotiation in the interprofessional context. You will explore trust and how to build trust and respect for colleagues and other health professionals, the person(s) receiving care, and their care team. · In Module Two you will develop the skills to communicate effectively with team members and appreciate the consequences when communication breaks down and is ineffective. This includes the role of communication in patient safety, handovers and transitions of care, health literacy, and communicating with diverse patient and population groups. · In Module Three, you explore team functioning, including barriers and enablers, consumer perspectives on team functioning in healthcare, and the psychosocial hazards which impact team functioning. You will also follow the healthcare journey of a client across the three modules. Learning outcomes: L06

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 3 To Week 4 (10 Aug - 23 Aug)
learning_activities.topic: Practical sessions on professional clinical practice, digital health and electrophysical agents Practicals on professional clinical practice, telehealth, digital technologies and electrophysical agents will be held in person on campus during Weeks 1, 3-4, 8-13 of the semester. Each session will run for 2 hours and will incorporate inquiry-based learning and small group discussions to explore key concepts in greater depth. These sessions are designed as experiential learning activities, and participants are expected to attend and actively engage. To prepare, participants must complete the associated online self-paced learning modules and preparation tasks before each tutorial. As these sessions involve small group work, they will not be recorded. Learning outcomes: L02, L04, L05
Physiotherapy Panel Tutorial This is a 2-hour live online tutorial that will involve group discussions. Learning outcomes: L03, L04, L06

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 6 To Week 7 (31 Aug - 13 Sep)
learning_activities.topic: Clinical observations Weeks 6-7: clinical visits. Students will attend a 2-hour clinical observation placement in either week 6 or 7. Details on available placement site and times will be provided via InPlace. Learning outcomes: L03, L04
